checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan Weft 0.6.0 colour-independent threads: give all nine colours a unique SVG dash pattern on the thread and spool ring, keep solid coral as the control, document the accessibility choice and verify the loom at desktop and mobile sizes

impact_assessment.why: Every thread and spool is identified by hue alone; a player with red-green or blue-purple colour vision deficiency cannot reliably match the nine pairs or follow a drawn path.
impact_assessment.benefits: A dash texture on each thread and its spool ring makes pairs and routes readable without colour, adds no asset, no setting and no storage, and keeps the existing glow aesthetic.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: SVG stroke-dasharray values on thread cores, drafts and spool rings; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: no save or schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep a unique pattern map with a unit test, leave coral solid as the baseline, choose patterns distinct from the existing draft and hint dashes, and review desktop and 390px screenshots before delivery

[1/4] Plan Weft 0.7.0 daily history: add a pure recent-days helper, render the last seven daily results as a compact strip under the daily card, test the rollover and states, and keep the history display-only so a streak cannot be back-filled

impact_assessment.why: The daily streak is a single number with no visible record, so a returning player cannot see which days were woven or how close the streak is to breaking.
impact_assessment.benefits: Seven days of results turn the streak into a legible habit, reuse the existing weft.daily.v1 data without a migration, and need no network or new asset.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the levels daily strip gains a list of seven day chips and the daily save module gains one pure helper; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: read-only over weft.daily.v1, no new storage key
impact_assessment.mitigation: Unit-test recentDays across month, year and count boundaries; keep today and past states distinct; dogfood the seven-chip strip after a real daily solve; review desktop and 390px renders

[1/4] Cycle 1: fix the post-victory dead end where Escape dismisses the win dialog, freezes the board and hides every next step; reopen the result from the won loom by pointer and keyboard, tell the player, and prove it with a before/after pair plus a played solve-dismiss-reopen-next run

impact_assessment.why: After a win, pressing Escape closes the victory dialog and leaves Undo/Reset/Hint disabled with no visible Next or Replay path; a real played run reproduced dialogOpen=false, frozen move count and no recovery affordance except Chambers.
impact_assessment.benefits: Keeps the finished tapestry inspectable while restoring a clear Next/Replay path, works for pointer and keyboard, adds no new control, no save change and no new dependency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: win-dialog close handler and beginDraft won branch; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: no save schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first browser dogfood assertion records the pre-fix dead end, before/after screenshots at 1440x900 from the same fresh-profile first chamber, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood after the fix, explicit staging, no push
